GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2018-10-04T23:34:08Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Sound stop after a while when looping
Description: ### Issue description

Using ExoPlayer 2.8.2 to play a local .m4a sound file in repeat mode, the sound stop after a while (typically a couple of hours). If playing several files simultaneously, each file stop at a different time. No error is reported in neither the player event listener nor the media source event listener.

The error occurs with both `player.setRepeatMode(Player.REPEAT_MODE_ALL);` or by using a LoopingMediaSource object.

When the audio stop, the following lines appears in Logcat:
    1536-1577/? I/AudioFlinger: BUFFER TIMEOUT: remove(4096) from active list on thread 0xf1203680
    1430-1578/? W/audio_hw_generic: Not supplying enough data to HAL, expected position 942828484 , only wrote 934428960

toggling player.setPlayWhenReady(...) does not restore the playback.

We didn't notice this issue (and none of our users complain) with the previous version of ExoPlayer we were using: r2.4.1. Unfortunately it is not possible to roll back as an audio glitch was audible at the end of each loop.

### Reproduction steps

The following code is running in a service:

```
...
dataSourceFactory = new DefaultDataSourceFactory(context, Util.getUserAgent(context, "XXXX"), null);
player = ExoPlayerFactory.newSimpleInstance(context, new DefaultTrackSelector());
MediaSource audioSource = new ExtractorMediaSource.Factory(dataSourceFactory).createMediaSource(audioItem.getUri());
player.setRepeatMode(Player.REPEAT_MODE_ALL);
player.prepare(audioSource);
...
player.setPlayWhenReady(true);
```

Wait until the sound stops

### Link to test content
Sent by email

### Version of ExoPlayer being used
2.8.2

### Device(s) and version(s) of Android being used
Pixel XL simulator with Android Oreo 8.1
Some of our users complained about the same issue on different devices.

### A full bug report captured from the device
Sent by email
